To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the RFMD is able to describe low-energy elastic NN data and the cross sections for the processes of astrophysics interest; 2) the enhancement of the S_{pp}(o) value is due to the relativistic effects; 3) the cross sections for neutrino disintegration of the deuterium are in agreement with experimental data.
the relativistic field theoretical model of the deutron can be applied to describe the processes of the astrophysics interest and low energy elastic NN scattering.

we have developed a model that describes the low-energy elastic NN data and the astrophysical processes of interest, and that this model gives a better description of astrophysical processes than the potential model approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of a relativistic field theory approach to the description of low-energy NN scattering and processes of astrophysicall interest.
the application of a relativistic field theory of the deuteron to the description of low--energy NN scattering, the pep--process and the disintegration of deuteron by (antineutrinos) neutrinos.
the relativistic field theoretical description of low-energy processes in the deuteron and the astrophysical aspects related to these processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RFMD is in good agreement with the PPA results for processes of astrophysics interest.
the results obtained within the RFMD for the processes of astrophysiological and nuclear interest are in complete agreement with experimental data and with the PMA results.

the relativistic approach is superior to the non-relativistic one, at least in the case of the deuteron, because it provides a more complete description of the deuteron properties and processes involving the deuteron.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the RFMD is able to describe the deuteron structure and the low--energy NN scattering in agreement with the phenomenological approach and to calculate the astrophysically interesting processes of the deuteron disintegration by neutrinos and the pep process in agreement with the potential model results.
the relativistic field theoretical approach to nuclear processes is a promising one.

the results of our calculations for the deuteron disintegration by (anti-)neutrinos, pep-process and neutron-proton capture in the RFMD are in good agreement with phenomenological results obtained in the PMA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RFMD is able to describe the processes of interest in the field of solar and stellar astrophysics.
the relativistic field-theory approach is able to describe nuclear reactions of astrophysical importance and low-energy elastic nucleon-nucleon scattering with the same set of parameters.
the relativistic field-theoretic model of the deutron (RFMD) provides a more accurate description of the deuteron properties than the potential model approach.
